chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, who said:

I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Our companions mention that when the sun declines, the time for Dhuhr and Asr has entered, and when it sets, the time for Maghrib and the last Isha has entered, with this being earlier than that during travel and residence, and that the time for Maghrib is until a quarter of the night.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The timing is like that, except that the time for Maghrib is narrow, and its end is the departure of the redness and its turning to whiteness in the western horizon.'

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: Decline of the sun (start of Dhuhr time)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer end according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the scholarly distinction between the general opinion of the companions, who extended Maghrib time to a quarter of the night, and Imam Al-Reza’s (peace be upon him) more precise definition based on the disappearance of the red twilight (shafaq) in the western horizon. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the narrowness of the Maghrib window, ensuring prayers are offered at their optimal, prescribed moments rather than merely within a broad permissible range.
